title: LIBS elemental imager: design files, firmware and software
description:
Design files, firmware and software of a laboratory laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) elemental imager built from low-cost CNC-derived components, with a fully hardware-triggered acquisition chain. The sample moves under a fixed laser and fixed collection optics on three ball-screw linear stages driven by Grbl_ESP32. The step pulses of the scan axis are counted and divided by an Arduino-based pulse controller that triggers the laser, which in turn triggers six fiber-coupled spectrometers, so shot spacing is locked to stage position rather than to software timing. A Python/PyQt5 application writes compressed NetCDF4 hyperspectral cubes; a second application turns them into elemental maps, ratios and RGB composites.

This record is the software and design archive of the HardwareX article A Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) elemental imager built from CNC-derived components with a fully hardware-triggered acquisition chain.

Licensing is per file and machine-readable in REUSE.toml: CAD under CERN-OHL-W-2.0, firmware and software under GPL-3.0-only, documentation and tables under CC-BY-4.0. Two exceptions, the Avantes SDK wrapper and the institutional logos, are described in LICENSING.md.

Developed at the Geological Survey of Belgium (Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences) within the BELSPO BRAIN-be projects LIBSCREEN and LEAP.
